candidates.name: baseline
candidates.what: the unchanged pipeline, whose own edge is displaced by the missing samples

candidates.name: dense_nearest
candidates.what: fills from the nearest sample, which lands on the wrong surface near the edge

candidates.name: broad_interpolation
candidates.what: averages across the step, which is the flying-pixel geometry itself

candidates.name: foreground_bias
candidates.what: prefers the nearer surface among nearby samples, which walks the step outward

candidates.name: spatial_completion
candidates.what: the product primitive at a depth edge: it recovers the isolated speckle away from the boundary and refuses the whole edge band, which is one connected region spanning the frame. Nothing is bridged and nothing is misplaced, and the step the missing samples displaced is still displaced - the honest remaining failure, and one another view has to fix

candidates.name: easy_samples_only
candidates.what: fills only the easy holes and leaves the edge alone

candidates.name: forged_measured_states
candidates.what: reports every reconstructed sample as a camera measurement

gates.context: the acceptance target: this fraction of the window must end up measured, or reconstructed onto surface that is really there. 0.95 of the surface this scene actually has; the unchanged baseline does not reach it, which is the whole reason this thread exists
gates.name: coverage.supported_fraction

gates.context: non-inferiority: the raw measurements the sensor did return must all still be there and still be called measurements. A completion that discards awkward samples and interpolates over them is not a completion
gates.name: coverage.measured_fraction

gates.context: absolute: 4 raw codes. Error is scored ONLY on samples the candidate reconstructed where truth was held out, so copying the input cannot earn a good score here, and the coverage gates stop a candidate improving this by reconstructing only the easy holes
gates.name: reconstructed_depth.p95
gates.unit: synthetic depth units: raw code x depth scale, exact by construction

gates.context: absolute: 16 raw codes. A single sample placed on the wrong surface is the failure a percentile hides
gates.name: reconstructed_depth.worst
gates.unit: synthetic depth units: raw code x depth scale, exact by construction

gates.context: absolute: zero. A reconstructed sample in the empty band between the foreground and the background is a flying pixel, whatever produced it
gates.name: edge.bridging

gates.context: absolute: zero. A reconstructed sample on the wrong side of the step has been put on a surface it is not on
gates.name: edge.misplaced

gates.context: absolute: 1.0 column. The step belongs where the truth puts it. The baseline fails this gate on purpose - dropout along the edge moves its apparent boundary inward, which is exactly the defect completion should repair
gates.name: edge_step_column.worst

gates.context: non-inferiority: the baseline's own worst extent error plus 8 raw codes. Smoothing an object smaller is the classic way a denser result looks better and measures worse
gates.name: dimensions.worst
gates.unit: synthetic depth units: raw code x depth scale, exact by construction

gates.context: a strict gain, stated by this scene and not by any candidate: 54 sample(s) of this frame were dropped with a returned measurement on all four sides of them, on geometry that is locally planar, and a completion must recover at least that many onto surface that is really there. Beside coverage.measured_fraction, which pins the measured population, this is a strict supported-coverage gain over the unchanged baseline - which recovers none of them
gates.name: coverage.local_recovery

gates.context: absolute: 16 raw codes, the same worst-sample tolerance the held-out error gate uses, applied only to reconstructions the candidate itself published at confidence 0.5 or above. A completion is free to be unsure; what it may not do is be sure and wrong. Lowering its own confidence is the only way to leave this gate, and that lowering is visible in the same measurement
gates.name: confidence.high_confidence_worst
gates.unit: synthetic depth units: raw code x depth scale, exact by construction

gates.context: the work a completion spent must be inside the budget derivable from its input before it ran - one neighbourhood scan per hole at its published radius. A bound by construction rather than a wall-clock assertion, which would measure the machine. Candidates that report no work record leave this gate inapplicable, and each case declares exactly which ones those are
gates.name: completion_work.within_budget

notes: The edge-band mask removes the samples on both sides of the boundary, which is why the BASELINE fails the step-column gate: with its edge samples gone, the apparent step is displaced inward. That is a real defect and the one a completion is supposed to repair - not an accident of the fixture.
'Bridging' counts reconstructed samples in the empty band between the two surfaces; 'misplaced' counts samples put on the wrong side of the step.
what: A box in front of a backing plane, with dropout hugging the depth edge.
why: The failure this whole thread exists to prevent. Dropout is worst exactly where the geometry is most discontinuous, so a completion is most tempted to interpolate precisely where interpolation is meaningless.
